bull.b: Very low debt-to-equity (~0.04) materially reduces financial distress risk and preserves borrowing capacity. This structural strength gives management flexibility to fund R&D or partnerships without high interest burden, supporting sustained clinical execution over months.

A $275M private placement specifically earmarked to start a registrational Phase 3 for EB613 materially reduces near-term execution risk. The financing also brings strategic institutional investors and board representation, strengthening governance and long-term program support.

Owning an oral peptide delivery platform targets a durable commercial pain point versus injectables. Progress on EB613 and a 50/50 OPKO tie-up on EB612 diversifies development risk and leverages partner resources, strengthening the firm's long-term product and go-to-market prospects.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating cash flow (~-$21.9M TTM) and FCF (~-$22.0M) indicate cash consumption is substantive and worsening. This structural cash drain increases dependency on external financing and constrains discretionary R&D or commercial investments absent further capital.

A pre-commercial profile with $0 TTM revenue and recurring losses means value creation depends entirely on successful trials and approvals. This structural lack of operating cash inflows prolongs reliance on external capital and heightens binary clinical and regulatory risks for long-term viability.

bear.t: High dilution capacity / shareholder dilution risk
bear.b: Expanding authorized shares and recent large equity issuance plus warrants materially raise dilution capacity. Reliance on equity financings to fund development can erode existing shareholders' stakes and per-share economics, a structural governance and financing risk going forward.
